thread:
alex: Heads-up — customer `acme` opened a severity-2 ticket, reporting a big p95/p99 jump on the text-gen API in us-east-1 since ~03:15 UTC. Small payloads only (~20–60 tokens). p95 went from ~120ms -> 360ms, p99 from ~280ms -> 920ms.

maria: Oof. Any deploys around that time?

jordan: Nope no infra deploys logged in that window. But I see a config rollout to continuous-batcher v2 on a few pools at 03:10 (canary -> region).

alex: Correlates. I pulled the span traces — tail latency concentrated in the batcher wait path. Lots of tiny reqs being coalesced into large batches (batch sizes hitting 64) which then sit on a 30ms grace timer waiting for more.

sam: Do we have metrics for hold-window / batch-timeout per pool?

jordan: Yes — sample from worker-12 in us-east-1: `batch_size.count.p50=4 p90=24 p99=58`, `batcher.grace_ms=30`, `batcher.max_batch_size=64`, `batcher.early_flush_threshold=0.05` (disabled effectively).

maria: That explains the small payload penalty — tiny requests getting stuck behind greedy coalescing. We should either reduce grace_ms or lower max_batch_size for tenant-local routes.

alex: Immediate mitigation options: 1) tenant override to disable batching for `acme` 2) per-pool config tweak (reduce grace_ms to 8ms + max_batch_size=16) 3) route `acme` to dedicated small-payload pool. Which is fastest?

sam: Tenant override is quickest. I can flip it. Command I use: 
```
curl -X POST "https://internal-console.redwood/api/admin/tenants/acme/overrides" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"allow_batching": false, "note":"hotfix 1787654321"}'
```

ops-bot: deploy-notify: tenant-override applied for `acme` by sam at 1787654800 (propagated to us-east-1 pools).

alex: Sam — after the override, did p95/p99 drop?

sam: Monitoring now — within 2 minutes p95 back to ~140ms, p99 ~310ms for acme. Ticket owner confirmed response times much better.

jordan: Good. We should still make a safer config default. Proposed follow-up: revert global continuous-batcher rollout and re-run canary with `grace_ms=8` and `max_batch_size=16` and `early_flush_threshold=0.15`. Also add an auto-detect rule: if median payload tokens < 80, prefer small-payload pool or lower batching aggressiveness.

maria: Agree. Also add an alert for batcher.p99 > baseline*2 so we catch regressions quicker.

alex: Action items: 
- sam: keep tenant override for now and monitor for 1h (done).
- jordan + maria: cut a rollback OR patch rollout with new defaults, run canary against small-payload traffic (ETA 2h).
- ops: add alert rule and a quick runbook entry for tenant override (who can flip, required approvals).

sam: I'll keep the thread updated. If rollback needed I can trigger it.

alex: Thanks. Save repro steps for postmortem: how to reproduce locally (gateway -> inject tiny requests at 2k rps, set grace_ms 30, max_batch_size 64) + traces.

jordan: Noted — I'll capture the traces and link them to the ticket.

maria: Nice fast triage team. :thumbsup:
